commodity: Mixed light-REE oxides (Ce, La, Nd, Pr)
geology: Fluorocarbonate; main LREE ore. Mountain Pass (California) carbonatite and Bayan Obo (Inner Mongolia, China) where it occurs with iron ore and monazite (bastnäsite:monazite ~9:1 to 1:1). ~65-75% REO.
intermediate: ~60% REO flotation concentrate -> roasted/calcined -> acid or alkaline leach -> mixed RE chloride/nitrate liquor
extraction: Roasting/Calcination to drive off CO2 and oxidize Ce, then Leaching to solution, then multi-stage SolventExtraction cascade to individual REO, then MoltenSaltElectrolysis to metal
final_product: Individual light-REE metals (La, Ce, Pr, Nd); NdPr feed for NdFeB magnets
notes: Flagship LREE ore. Comes out as a MIXED concentrate - element separation happens later in the SX cascade, not in beneficiation. Low Th compared to monazite.

geology: REE phosphate; dense and paramagnetic, concentrates in heavy-mineral sands and carbonatites. LREE-dominant but notable Nd. ~55-60% REO. Carries 5-10%+ ThO2 -> radioactive handling required.
intermediate: RE phosphate cracked by hot NaOH (AlkalineBake, 120-175 C) or H2SO4 (AcidBake, 200-300 C) -> dissolve -> precipitate Th(OH)4 out -> mixed RE liquor
extraction: Cracking(AlkalineBake or AcidBake) to destroy phosphate matrix and liberate Th + REEs, dissolution, selective Th removal, then SolventExtraction cascade to individual REO, then electrolysis / Ca reduction
final_product: Individual light-REE metals; thorium precipitate sequestered/stored
notes: Also a thorium source. Radioactivity/Th handling is mandatory and gameplay-relevant: Th(OH)4 is selectively precipitated (pH control with NaOH/NH4OH) before REEs proceed. Cross-links to the minor/radioactive group (Th).

commodity: Heavy-REE-enriched oxides (Y, Dy, Yb, Er, Gd)
geology: Yttrium phosphate, isostructural with zircon; heavy-REE enriched (Y plus mid/heavy lanthanides substitute for Y). Found in placers and granitic pegmatites. ~54-65% REO.
intermediate: Hot NaOH or H2SO4 bake (more refractory than monazite) -> dissolve -> mixed HRE liquor
extraction: Cracking(AlkalineBake/AcidBake), Leaching, then the hardest SolventExtraction separations (adjacent heavy REEs), then MetallothermicReduction(Ca) or electrolysis
final_product: Y, Dy, Tb, Er, Gd oxides and metals
notes: Primary hard-rock source of heavy REEs. Heavy-REE separations in the SX cascade are the most difficult of all.

formula: REE3+ adsorbed on kaolinite/halloysite/illite (no discrete REE mineral)
commodity: Heavy REEs incl. Dy, Tb, Y (plus some LREE)
geology: Regolith-hosted deposits from weathering of granite, latitudes ~24-26 N in South China. REE3+ ions loosely adsorbed on clay surfaces - NOT a mineral lattice. Accounts for >80% of world medium/heavy REE supply; the dominant Dy/Tb/Y source.
intermediate: In-situ / heap IonExchange leach with (NH4)2SO4 or NaCl displaces REE3+ into solution -> RE sulfate/chloride liquor -> Precipitation (oxalate/carbonate)
extraction: IonExchange leach (no crushing or flotation needed - ions are simply exchanged off the clay), Precipitation, then SolventExtraction cascade to individual heavy REO
final_product: Dy, Tb, Y oxides -> heavy-REE magnet additives and phosphors
notes: The cheap, simple-to-mine but strategically vital heavy-REE source. No frothflotation/grinding - highlights that the separation (SX cascade of Dy/Tb) is the hard part, not extraction from the clay.

geology: Complex perovskite-type oxide; Kola Peninsula (Russia) alkaline massifs. Mined mainly for Ti/Nb/Ta, with REEs as a by-product.
intermediate: Chlorination / acid crack -> separate Ti,Nb,Ta -> RE liquor
extraction: Cracking, Leaching, SolventExtraction for the LREE byproduct stream
notes: Brief coverage - REE is a co-product here. Carries Th (radioactive group).

geology: Brownish-black complex oxide in granitic pegmatites; Nb/Ta-dominant (vs Ti-dominant polycrase). Radioactive (U, Th).
intermediate: Acid or alkaline crack -> RE + Nb/Ta liquor
notes: Brief coverage. Radioactive U/Th present - links to the minor/radioactive group.

geology: Separated from mixed LREE concentrate (bastnäsite/monazite) by the SX cascade; co-produced with Pr as NdPr.
extraction: From mixed RE liquor: SolventExtraction to isolate Nd, Precipitation (oxalate), Calcination to Nd2O3, then MoltenSaltElectrolysis in a molten NdF3-LiF fluoride bath (~1050 C); iron cathode can yield Nd-Fe alloy directly
notes: The flagship magnet metal. NdFeB = Nd + Pr + Fe + B, with Dy/Tb added for high-temperature coercivity. Main demand driver (EV motors, wind turbines).

geology: Separated from mixed LREE concentrate; usually co-produced with Nd as 'NdPr' / didymium.
extraction: SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to Pr6O11, MoltenSaltElectrolysis
notes: Magnet metal, typically sold/used together with Nd (NdPr) - the two are hard to fully separate and share end use.

geology: Heavy REE - mainly from ion-adsorption clays and xenotime. One of the HARDEST and most valuable separations.
extraction: Many-stage SolventExtraction (hardest heavy separations), Precipitation, Calcination to Dy2O3, MetallothermicReduction(Ca) of the fluoride
notes: Critical NdFeB additive - keeps magnets coercive at high temperature. Its separation difficulty (adjacent heavy REEs) is the economic crux of the whole chain.

geology: Mid/light-heavy boundary REE, separated from mixed LREE concentrate.
extraction: SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to Sm2O3, MetallothermicReduction(Ca) (Sm is volatile - reduced with La/Ca, not easily electrowon)
notes: SmCo magnets (Sm + Co) for very high temperature / aerospace & defence applications.

geology: Lightest REE, abundant in bastnäsite/monazite; comes off early in the SX cascade.
extraction: SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to La2O3, MoltenSaltElectrolysis
notes: FCC petroleum-cracking catalysts and NiMH battery alloys. Cheap, high-volume.

geology: Most abundant REE; easily split off because Ce can be oxidized to Ce(IV) and removed selectively.
extraction: Oxidative separation / SolventExtraction, Precipitation, Calcination to CeO2 (often used as oxide directly)
notes: Glass polishing, auto-exhaust catalysts, UV-absorbing glass. The Ce(IV) oxidation trick makes it the easiest REE to pull out of the mix.

geology: Scarce mid-REE; separable via its reducible Eu(II) state (reduce to Eu2+, precipitate as sulfate).
extraction: SolventExtraction / Eu(II) reduction-precipitation, Calcination to Eu2O3
notes: Red and blue phosphors (displays, fluorescent lighting). High value, low volume.

geology: Grouped with the heavy REEs; dominant element in xenotime and major component of ion-adsorption clays.
extraction: SolventExtraction / IonExchange, Precipitation, Calcination to Y2O3, MetallothermicReduction(Ca)
notes: Phosphor host lattice, YAG, high-temperature ceramics. Behaves as a heavy REE despite low atomic number.

geology: Heavy REE from ion-adsorption clays and xenotime; one of the scarcest and hardest to separate.
extraction: Many-stage SolventExtraction (very hard heavy separation), Precipitation, Calcination to Tb4O7, MetallothermicReduction(Ca)
notes: Magnet additive (like Dy) plus green phosphor. Extremely scarce and expensive - the difficulty of its separation is a core gameplay hook.
